textbookText: Figure: 1 mol of carbon=12 g.
Different ways of expressing numbers 1 dozen =12 pieces 1 gross =144 pieces 1 ream =500 pieces 1 mol = 6.022x1023 particles
One mol is defined as the number of atoms as there are in exactly 12 g of carbon -12.

One mol contains 6.022×1023 particles. This number (6.022×1023) is referred to as Avogadro’s number (NA) named in honor of Amedeo Avogadro, a pioneer investigator of the quantitative aspects of chemistry.
1 mol = 6.022×1023 (atoms, ions or molecules)

Mol of substance can be converted in to number of particles (molecules, atoms, ions or electron) by multiplying with Avogadro’s number (NA) whereas number of particles can be converted into mol by dividing with Avogadro’s number (NA).
Do you know how big is Avogadro’s number?
If you started contains now at the rate of 10 billion atoms per second it will take 2 billion years to count the Avogadro’s number
Number of mol = 6.022𝑥 1023 𝑛𝑢𝑚𝑏𝑒𝑟 𝑜𝑓 𝑝𝑎𝑟𝑡𝑖𝑐𝑙𝑒𝑠
Equal number of mol contains an equal number of particles. Therefore, 12 g of carbon and 63.5 g of copper contain same number of particles (6.022×1023) .
Do you know? The number of molcules in a single droplet of water is roughly 100 billion times greater than the number of people on earth.

Solved problem Calculate the number of molecules, number of atoms and number of electrons in 0.5 mol of water. Solution, Number of molecules of water = number of mol× NA =0.5 6.022x1023 =3.011 ×1023 Since one molecule of water contains three atoms Number of atoms =number of molecules × 3 = 3.011 x1023×3 = 9.033×1023 Likewise, one molecule of water contains 10 electrons Number of electrons in 0.5 mol of water = number of molecules ×10 = 3.011 ×1023×10 = 3.011 ×1024 Test yourself!
